title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier with a bounded automated repair budget increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic NetOps validator. Each paired intent produced one shared_initial generation that was evaluated under two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation and ≤1 automated repair). Outcomes: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We archive preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policies.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are rapidly being applied to NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment network changes, semantic correctness properties—sequencing constraints, reachability, and policy preservation—are operationally critical and cannot be assured by superficial syntactic checks alone. A common engineering pattern pairs generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce operational risk. The measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends on the experimental estimand (what is held fixed), the single‑draw quality of the generator, the validator's expressiveness, and the permitted repair budget.

We preregistered a paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) to quantify the bounded deterministic rescue achievable when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate using the declared generator (gpt-5-mini) and compared: (a) baseline—accept the single candidate without repair; and (b) guarded—run a deterministic validator and allow at most one automated repair which itself is re‑validated. The primary research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair?

Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a shared_initial estimand that conditions on one LLM draw per intent; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the single automated repair transcript archived with the run; and (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of estimator conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and system papers document active application of LLMs to NetOps tasks including intent translation, configuration synthesis, automated testing, and repair [1–4]. A parallel literature explores tool‑augmented agent architectures (planner‑centric, ReAct, and related frameworks) that let LLMs call external validators or simulators to decompose multi‑step workflows and coordinate tool outputs [5,6]. Empirical reports indicate that deterministic checks and generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve surface correctness relative to unconstrained generation, but reported gains vary strongly with validator coverage, task distribution, and whether pipelines permit resampling or interactive steering [2,3].

Two methodological themes motivate our design. First, evaluations that conflate deterministic validation with benefits from multiple independent model draws make it difficult to bound rescue attributable solely to post‑generation checking; isolating a shared_initial draw avoids that conflation [2]. Second, many publicly available NetOps benchmarks emphasize syntactic/template correctness rather than semantically rich invariants (reachability, sequencing, policy preservation), which limits operational generality of claims; several works call for verifier‑centric benchmarks but community adoption remains incomplete [4,7]. Our study positions itself explicitly within these threads by conditioning on a single LLM candidate and measuring only bounded, deterministic repair.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the confirmatory design under study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001 (preregistration archived) and fixed the primary estimand as the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) on N = 300 paired intents after applying prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The confirmatory analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1) and multiplicity handling were fixed prior to the main run.

Task generation and stratification. Tasks were produced deterministically by a registered synthetic task generator into a topology suite stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high). Each task manifest encodes the natural‑language intent, initial and expected final device states, ordering constraints (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), preservation invariants, and protected interfaces. The confirmatory run sampled 100 pairs per stratum.

Shared_initial protocol and model configuration. To isolate deterministic validator/repair rescue from generator resampling effects we implemented the shared_initial estimand: for each pair the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate reused verbatim for both baseline and guarded conditions. The declared generation model was gpt-5-mini (execution configuration records requested_model = "gpt-5-mini"). Reusing the same candidate across conditions prevents differences due to additional independent draws and measures only deterministic validation and bounded repair applied to the identical output.

Deterministic validator and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic NetOps validator implementing a full_intent_constraint_validation rule that checks sequencing invariants, required_command_count, preservation of unspecified state, reachability invariants encoded by the synthetic suite, and forbidden‑template protections for protected interfaces. Scoring is binary: an unflagged candidate is a pass for the estimand. The guarded pipeline permits at most one automated repair attempt (repair budget ≤ 1). The repair operator is a constrained edit routine limited to localized sequencing and insertion edits (for example, inserting a missing "admin down" before a VLAN/MTU change). Repairs are applied only if the validator flags the shared_initial candidate; repair attempts are re‑validated deterministically.

Contamination controls, exclusions, and stopping rule. The preregistration included deterministic contamination detection and one negative control per stratum. A pair would be excluded from confirmatory analysis only if both pipeline calls failed due to provider/infrastructure outage. The stopping rule halted execution if >20% of attempted pairs were excluded due to dual‑call outages. The run completed without excluded pairs.

Execution auditing and reproducibility pointer. The run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter in scientific_confirmatory mode. Execution accounting and stage counts are archived with the run. For reproducibility we direct readers to the archived run bundle and execution manifest (manifest path: execution/execution_manifest.json; representative manifest artifact hash: 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). The preregistration, task manifests, validator traces, repair trace, raw responses, and analysis inputs are included in the archive.
sections.results:
Execution integrity. The adapter completed the confirmatory run with completed_episode_count = 600, yielding complete_pair_count = 300 paired observations under the shared_initial protocol. Provider/audit records show hosted_model_call_event_count = 301 (300 shared_initial generations plus one repair invocation). Deterministic reconciliation confirmed consistent episode accounting and the absence of provider/infrastructure failures or excluded pairs.

Primary outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00, 0.01]. Because discordance is minimal (m = n10 + n01 = 1), the exact test has limited sensitivity and the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point in this experimental context.

Per‑stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per stratum tallies were: low baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100 and guarded = 100/100. All discordant evidence was concentrated in one hard example in the high stratum. That solitary discordant pair invoked the permitted automated repair: validator traces attribute the initial failure to a sequencing invariant omission (a missing explicit "admin down" before a VLAN/MTU change). The constrained repair performed a single localized insertion; re‑validation reported valid == true for the corrected candidate. The repair therefore produced a deterministic rescue with one additional repair stage call.

Cost footprint. The guarded pipeline caused a single additional repair stage call across 300 pairs (model_calls_used = 301), indicating a negligible marginal model‑call cost for deterministic rescue in this run.

Statistical interpretation. The confirmatory inferential outcome (p = 1.0) primarily reflects the paucity of discordant pairs under the shared_initial estimand and selected synthetic suite. Exact McNemar inference depends only on n10 and n01; with n10 = 1 and n01 = 0 the two‑sided exact p equals 1.0, indicating no statistically detectable difference under conventional two‑sided testing in this sample. The paired bootstrap CI provides an effect‑size bound: given observed data and preregistered estimand, the absolute paired improvement is plausibly between 0 and 0.01. These inferences apply strictly to the shared_initial conditioning (one LLM draw reused across conditions), the limited repair budget (≤1 constrained edit), the synthetic task distribution, and the declared generator and validator.
sections.discussion:
Estimand and operational alignment. Conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent corresponds to operational policies that constrain model calls for cost, latency, or governance. Under such policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. Workflows that permit resampling, verifier‑guided generation, or interactive steering change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates by exploiting generator variance; those workflows require different preregistered designs.

Ceiling effects and pilot omission. The preregistration targeted detecting a 10 percentage‑point absolute improvement with power ≈0.8 based on a planned pilot to estimate discordance. The optional pilot (n = 60) was not executed; the main run encountered a near‑ceiling baseline (299/300), producing minimal discordance (m = 1) and reducing power to detect small absolute differences. This underscores the utility of small calibration pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling on the chosen suite.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The observed failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, ACL removal) were not observed at scale in this synthetic suite. The marginal utility of a guarded pipeline therefore depends on (a) the deployment distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness. Richer validators that detect reachability or ACL semantics may increase observed rescue rates; conversely, operator policies that disallow automated edits limit the guarded pipeline to detection and human escalation.

Repair budget tradeoffs. We intentionally limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to measure bounded deterministic rescue. Iterative repair, larger edit operators, or interactive verifier‑guided regeneration would increase rescue opportunities but measure a different estimand and impose higher model‑call budgets. The archived single repair trace enables analysis of edit efficacy and can inform permitted edit‑operator design in production pipelines.

Operational guidance. If deployment policies tightly budget model calls, the shared_initial estimand provides an operationally meaningful bound for deterministic verifier/repair rescue applied to a single candidate. If policies permit resampling or interactive steering, evaluations should allow resampling to measure the achievable success rates under those policies.
sections.conclusion: We ran a preregistered paired comparison between a verifier‑assisted pipeline (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair) and accepting a single‑shot LLM candidate under the shared_initial estimand on 300 synthetic NetOps intents using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. Baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 unflagged verifier passes and the guarded pipeline 300/300, yielding an absolute paired improvement of 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). Deterministic validator+repair rescued a single sequencing omission under the bounded repair budget. The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity to small absolute improvements under the shared_initial estimand. We release full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility and targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, or repair budget.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and the reported deterministic validator were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
